logline: An Anglo-Indian Kolkata detective investigates the murder of a teenager from a powerful family while battling her own demons, in a noir thriller adapted from the novel City of Death.

renewal.note: Seven-episode limited series adapted from a standalone novel. No Season 2 announced.

bollymeter.basis: Atmospheric Kolkata noir elevated by a committed Karisma Kapoor, undercut by a sluggish pace and a predictable murder-mystery that delivers no surprises in seven episodes.

pull_quotes.text: Karisma Kapoor is very watchable, but her Rita Brown is too much of a literary formula to make a dent.
Brown tries to balance atmospheric depth with a sluggish plot, and the balance does not always hold.

seasons.review_body: Brown arrived carrying the weight of a major Karisma Kapoor comeback and the atmospheric promise of Kolkata noir. Critics landed in a familiar split: the performance camp found her uninhibited and physically committed, genuinely shedding the glitzy legacy. The craft camp noted that director Abhinay Deo builds a richly textured world, only to let it sink under a standard premise and a pacing that tests patience across seven episodes. The murder mystery offers no real surprises, and reviewers across outlets flagged cliches and formula. What rescues it from a skip is the texture of the setting and the lead performance. The reception settled as mixed-to-slightly-positive, with most critics recommending it as a one-time watch for Kapoor fans rather than a standout thriller on its own terms.
